severityScale.label: Not a usability problem
severityScale.description: I don't agree that this is a usability problem at all

severityScale.label: Cosmetic
severityScale.description: Cosmetic problem only; fix if time allows

severityScale.label: Catastrophic
severityScale.description: Usability catastrophe; must fix before release

heuristics.title: Visibility of system status
heuristics.description: The system should always keep users informed about what is going on, through appropriate feedback within reasonable time.

heuristics.title: Match between system and the real world
heuristics.description: The system should speak the users' language, with words, phrases, and concepts familiar to the user, rather than system-oriented terms.

heuristics.title: User control and freedom
heuristics.description: Users often choose system functions by mistake and will need a clearly marked emergency exit to leave the unwanted state without having to go through an extended dialogue.

heuristics.title: Consistency and standards
heuristics.description: Users should not have to wonder whether different words, situations, or actions mean the same thing. Follow platform conventions.

heuristics.title: Error prevention
heuristics.description: Even better than good error messages is a careful design which prevents a problem from occurring in the first place.

heuristics.title: Recognition rather than recall
heuristics.description: Minimise the user's memory load by making objects, actions, and options visible. The user should not have to remember information from one part of the dialogue to another.

heuristics.title: Flexibility and efficiency of use
heuristics.description: Accelerators — unseen by the novice user — may often speed up the interaction for the expert user such that the system can cater to both inexperienced and experienced users.

heuristics.title: Aesthetic and minimalist design
heuristics.description: Dialogues should not contain irrelevant or rarely needed information. Every extra unit of information in a dialogue competes with the relevant units of information and diminishes their relative visibility.

heuristics.title: Help users recognise, diagnose, and recover from errors
heuristics.description: Error messages should be expressed in plain language (no codes), precisely indicate the problem, and constructively suggest a solution.

heuristics.title: Help and documentation
heuristics.description: Even though it is better if the system can be used without documentation, it may be necessary to provide help and documentation. Any such information should be easy to search, focused on the user's task, and not be too large.
